requirement.title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement.text:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story: Adds a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] attribute. The source generator writes the body of a partial IMessagePackFormatter<T> class for a type T that has no MessagePack attributes, either contractless or keyed by an optional compile-time surrogate type. The change also adds diagnostics MsgPack019 through MsgPack022, docs and tests.

decisions.title: Dependency change in Directory.Packages.props
decisions.oneliner: Dependency and toolchain versions decide which users can build and run the package.
decisions.question: Accept this dependency or toolchain change?
decisions.routed_by: policy rule 'dependency': the reviewer may not decide this

decisions.title: Public API change in Attributes.cs
decisions.oneliner: New public types become a promise to every user of the package and cannot be removed without a breaking release.
decisions.question: Add GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute to the public API?
decisions.routed_by: policy rule 'public-api': the reviewer may not decide this

decisions.title: No check for two formatters of the same type
decisions.oneliner: If T already has [MessagePackObject] or a second generated formatter, both get registered in GeneratedMessagePackResolver. Nothing detects or reports the clash.
decisions.would_be_wrong_if: The model merge or the resolver template already deduplicates by data type or reports a diagnostic. That code is outside this diff.
decisions.question: Should a duplicate formatter for the same type be reported as an error?

handled.title: Some diagnostics may be missing message arguments
handled.oneliner: Existing descriptors are reused with no message arguments. If their messages contain {0}, the reported text will be broken or formatting may fail.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: The existing NoDeserializingConstructor, DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys and KeysMustBeUnique messages have no format placeholders.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Pipeline keeps symbols and runs Collect twice
handled.oneliner: GeneratedFormatterRequest holds INamedTypeSymbol, so incremental caching never hits. Collect also runs once for the model and once for diagnostics on every compilation.
quote: public sealed record GeneratedFormatterRequest(INamedTypeSymbol Formatter, INamedTypeSymbol? Surrogate);
handled.would_be_wrong_if: The existing pipelines already pass symbols this way and the IDE cost has been accepted.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Analyzer declares MsgPack019-022 but never reports them
handled.oneliner: Only the generator reports these. They are added to the analyzer's SupportedDiagnostics, but no analyzer action produces them.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: The truncated part of the diff adds analyzer actions that report these IDs.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Several rejection paths and map mode are untested
handled.oneliner: Nothing tests no-parameterless-constructor, generic data types, init-only or required members, or duplicate keys. The map-mode test project excludes the new tests.
quote: <!-- GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypes*.cs need the ExternalTypes assembly, which this project does not reference. -->
handled.would_be_wrong_if: Those paths are tested elsewhere, outside this diff.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

dropped.title: Surrogate design differs from the requested options
dropped.dropped_because: quote not found in diff: ['Only classes and structs are supported. Generic types, abstract types, and unions from other assemblies are not.']

Whether the generated resolver instantiates a user formatter that has a non-public or parameterized constructor.
